# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–5 (Complete and Final – Updated 68)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Quenwick, Wilhaven, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Cheltenham, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return; now married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea's life mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window; solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations; Fred gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner; three boys only, youngest resembles grandfather

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony; had dismal precocity of poverty
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist; sings better than Amelia
- **Character**: Determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed since age eight when caught stealing jam; capable of calculated charm and intimacy
- **Joseph Sedley Romance Campaign**: Upon learning of Joseph Sedley's wealth, determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"; invited by Amelia; won over entire household through charming behavior; left alone with Joseph in drawing-room; occupied knitting green silk purse; established great confidence and intimacy; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music ended; continued presenting nosegays; Rebecca refused his request to sing citing low spirits; asked him to help finish green silk purse; Joseph seated tete-a-tete with killing expression, hands bound in green silk web; Rebecca thought "I might go farther, and fare worse"
- **At Vauxhall**: Took Jos's arm; sat by him on open carriage box; everyone expected marriage announcement; lost themselves in solitary walk among couples; at Moscow panorama, rude fellow treading on foot caused her to fall into Joseph's arms; Joseph told favorite Indian stories again (sixth time); at supper during inebriation, Jos clasped her round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; Rebecca started but could not get away hand
- **After Vauxhall - Rejection and Departure from Sedley Household**: George Osborne pushed Jos back into seat; Jos never came; household turned against Rebecca; Blenkinsop reported Rebecca reading Mrs. Sedley's letters and accessing trinket boxes; Pinner suspected Rebecca had taken Amelia's white ribbing; entire household (except Amelia) agreed Rebecca should depart speedily; accepted Amelia's generous presents with proper hesitation; received purse from Mr. Sedley; kissing his hand, asked to consider him kind protector; behavior affecting—Mr. Sedley blessed her, invited her to always come when in town
- **Journey to Queen's Crawley**: Immediately upon departure counted guineas and began planning; carriage passed through Gaunt Square into Great Gaunt Street, stopped at tall gloomy house with hatchment over middle drawing-room window; departed London by coach early morning with bandboxes; awakened at daybreak by charwoman; placed initially inside coach but at Leakington (where rain began heavily), forced to go outside as Sir Pitt is proprietor of coach and passenger wanted inside place; rode outside in rain for greater part of way; young gentleman from Cambridge College sheltered her kindly in one of his several great coats; young Cantab (called Master Jack) and guard both knew Sir Pitt well, laughed at him, called him "old screw" (stingy, avaricious); Master Jack promised to "flog 'em on to Squashmore" in revenge for Sir Pitt's slow driving with his horses; carriage and four splendid horses with armorial bearings awaited at Mudbury, four miles from Queen's Crawley; made entrance to baronet's park in state; fine avenue of mile long leading to house; woman at lodge-gate (over pillars which are serpent and dove, supporters of Crawley arms) made curtsies as she flung open old iron carved doors; now at Queen's Crawley estate
- **First Evening at Queen's Crawley**: Interrupted by Sir Pitt in night-cap and dressing-gown who seized her candle, said "No candles after eleven o'clock, Miss Becky"; called her "pretty little hussy"; threatened to come for candle every night unless she's in bed at eleven; Sir Pitt and Mr. Horrocks the butler left laughing; two immense bloodhounds let loose at night, yelling and howling at moon; Sir Pitt calls dog "Gorer" (killed a man, master of bull); calls mother dog "Aroarer" (too old to bite, formerly called Flora)
- **First Dinner at Queen's Crawley**: Half hour after arrival, great dinner-bell rung; came down with two pupils (very thin insignificant little chits of ten and eight years old); wore Amelia's dear muslin gown; to be treated as one of family except on company days when young ladies and she dine upstairs; assembled in little drawing-room where Lady Crawley sits

**Lady Crawley (Second) - Mother of Rebecca's Pupils** [NEW CHARACTER]
- Ironmonger's daughter; marriage thought great match; looked as if handsome once; eyes always weeping for loss of beauty; pale and meagre and high-shouldered; has not a word to say for herself, evidently; mother of the young ladies (ten and eight years old)

**Mr. Crawley (Stepson/Son from First Marriage)** [NEW CHARACTER]
- In full dress, pompous as undertaker; pale, thin, ugly, silent; thin legs, no chest; hay-coloured whiskers and straw-coloured hair; very picture of sainted mother over mantelpiece—Griselda of noble house of Binkie

**Joseph Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint, returned to Europe; has own lodgings, not with family
- Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres and opera; extremely talkative in man's society
- At Vauxhall: escorted Rebecca to dinner and gardens; at supper ordered waiters with majesty, made salad, uncorked Champagne, carved chickens, ate greater part of refreshments; insisted bowl of rack punch, drank entire contents; became inebriated, talked and laughed loudly, voluntarily sang in maudlin high key, became bold as lion, clasped Rebecca round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; continued drinking, making love, singing
- Post-Vauxhall: George Osborne pushed Jos back into seat; Jos kissed hand to retreating ladies hiccupping "Bless you!"; seized Dobbin's hand weeping, confided he adored Rebecca, broke her heart, would marry her next morning; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave, conveyed him home; next morning Jos groaned in severe agonies; George Osborne found him groaning on sofa; Dobbin already in room tending patient; Jos's valet Mr. Brush reported Jos "uncommon wild"
- Sent letter to Amelia apologizing for Vauxhall conduct, attributing to rack punch, announcing immediate departure for Cheltenham and later Scotland for several months; thus avoided formal proposal entirely; Jos fled town, leaving Rebecca's hopes dashed
- Old Mr. Sedley feels akin to contempt for son; says Joseph vain, selfish, lazy, effeminate

**Miss Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister; natural infirmity of tears; match-maker at heart; too good, too kind, doesn't know world
- Bred up for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with George at single instant when he asked her for music
- Discovered million of virtues in Rebecca; warmed into most tender friendship; showed her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl; entirely agreed with mother's changed opinion
- Parting with Rebecca: ransacked all drawers, cupboards, reticules, gimcrack boxes to select presents; went to Papa to beg he give his promised money to Rebecca instead; wept confidentially on Blenkinsop's shoulder about household suspicions; parting theatrical scene—one person earnest, other perfect performer; after tenderest caresses and pathetic tears with smelling-bottle; vowed to love Rebecca forever; received pathetic letter from Rebecca describing her arrival at Sir Pitt's

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; clever artist; bred up for purpose of marrying Amelia
- At Vauxhall: Paired with Amelia; at supper in mated pair; did not like rack punch; intervened with commotion, single push sent Jos back into seat; removed ladies in safety
- Post-Vauxhall: Found Jos groaning next morning; not pleased that family member into which he was marrying should make mesalliance with little nobody—little upstart governess; pursued advantage pitilessly; thought Jos milksop; mocked Jos relentlessly about behavior and romantic declarations; inspired distrust and hatred in Rebecca; laughed at her discomfited mien; when Rebecca came downstairs, continued liveliness and banter; told Amelia she must learn her station, called her helpless creature; said Amelia too good, too kind, doesn't know world; expressed manly compunction for unnecessary unkindness; his mockery and interference effectively discouraged Jos from pursuing proposal

**William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Son of merchant/grocer; father keeps shop "Figs & Rudge" on Thames Street, City; father became Alderman Dobbin, Colonel of City Light Horse, later knighted; Dobbin entered army
- School experience: Giant amongst boys at Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, mercilessly bullied; defended George Osborne by fighting Cuff; thirteen-round left-handed fight, eventually prevailed; character rose prodigiously in estimation; name "Figs" became respectable and popular
- At Vauxhall and post-Vauxhall: Asked by George to look after shawls; carried Amelia's white cashmere shawl; paid at door for whole party; found himself humming Amelia's tune she sang on stairs; realized he was forgotten, decided he would be de trop; walked away; while walking about gardens, stepped up to supper box in agitated state when commotion seemed inevitable; shouldered off crowd
- Jos's departure: Jos seized Dobbin's hand and confided secret of his loves; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave gardens and hastened him to Lambeth Palace; conveyed Jos into hackney-coach depositing him at lodgings; next morning found Jos groaning on sofa, good-naturedly tended patient; entreated Osborne to have mercy when he mocked Jos
- Emotional attachment: Found himself unconsciously humming Amelia's tune; emotional attachment to Amelia beginning to develop

**Sir Pitt Crawley, Baronet** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background and Ancestry**: Named after the great Commoner; son of Walpole Crawley, first Baronet, of Tape and Sealing-Wax Office in reign of George II (impeached for peculation); family tree includes John Churchill Crawley, Charles Stuart Barebones Crawley, Queen Elizabeth's Crawley (forked beard, armour)
- **Marriages and Children**: First married to Griselda/Grizzel, sixth daughter of Mungo Binkie, Lord Binkie; she brought two sons—Pitt (named after minister) and Rawdon Crawley (named from Prince of Wales's friend); many years after Grizzel's demise, Sir Pitt led Rosa, daughter of Mr. G. Dawson of Mudbury, to altar; by Rosa he had two daughters (aged ten and eight) for whom Rebecca Sharp now engaged as governess
- **Estate and Borough**: Owner of Queen's Crawley estate in Hants and Great Gaunt Street mansion in London; Queen's Crawley formerly erected by Queen Elizabeth after she was delighted with Hampshire beer; now "rotten borough" producing "good fifteen hundred a year"; family represented in Parliament constantly
- **Appearance**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar, very dirty man in old clothes and shabby old gaiters; smoking horrid pipe; shining bald head, leering red face, twinkling grey eyes, mouth perpetually on grin
- **Character and Behavior**: Speaks with country accent; incessantly discussing himself; swears a great deal; sometimes coarsest and vulgarest Hampshire accent; pronounces avenue as "EVENUE" and nothing as "NOTHINK"; does not disguise his qualities; proprietor of coach and horses; drives very slow; stingy, avaricious (called "old screw"); never gives money to anybody; characterization as old, stumpy, vulgar, dirty, in shabby gaiters, smokes horrid pipe, cooks his own horrid supper in saucepan
- **Lawsuits**: Involved in numerous cases—"Crawley, Bart. v. Snaffle" (plans to throw Snaffle over), "Podder and another versus Crawley, Bart.," "Overseers of Snaily parish against Crawley, Bart." (claims common land belongs to him not parish, willing to spend thousand guineas to win)
- **Estate Management**: Has Mr. Hodson, his hind from Mudbury; discusses distraining, selling up, draining and subsoiling, tenants and farming; Sam Miles caught poaching; Peter Bailey gone to workhouse; "Serve him right," said Sir Pitt; "him and his family has been cheating me on that farm these hundred and fifty years"
- **Parsonage Matters**: Has sold the presentation of the living; in fury swore if he ever caught 'em poaching on his ground, he'd transport 'em; told Hodson he won't let any of poacher's breed get the parsonage living; suggests two brothers (parson and himself presumably) at variance
- **Harshness with Children**: Ordered Mr. Hodson to rush upon two little boys gathering sticks in wood with his whip; roared "Pitch into 'em, Hodson, flog their little souls out, and bring 'em up to the house, the vagabonds; I'll commit 'em as sure as my name's Pitt"
- **Household Management at Night**: Walks about in night-cap and dressing-gown; seized Rebecca's candle saying no candles after eleven o'clock; called her "pretty little hussy"; threatened to come for candle every night unless she's in bed at eleven; lets loose two immense bloodhounds at night; calls one dog "Gorer" (killed man, master of bull), other "Aroarer" (too old to bite, formerly Flora)
- **Wife (Rosa) - Deceased**: Called by Sir Pitt "the dowager" and "Lady Crawley"; was close but valuable woman who saved him steward; had mouldy old sampler in bedroom; had two little family pictures (young lads in college gown and red soldier jacket); slept in great front bedroom of Great Gaunt Street house; now dead

**Mr. Hodson** (Hind from Mudbury)
- Sir Pitt's estate manager; discusses farming matters; jumped out of carriage at Sir Pitt's order to rush upon little boys gathering sticks; cracked whip on their shoulders at Sir Pitt's command; agreed Sir Pitt right about poaching breed not getting parsonage living

**Mrs. Tinker** (Old Charwoman)
- Keeps Sir Pitt's Great Gaunt Street house; on board wages when Sir Pitt absent, dines with family when in town; shared supper of tripe and onion with Sir Pitt; sleeps with rushlight; leads Rebecca through house; said prayers before bed; would not be pumped by Rebecca for information

**Mr. Horrocks** (Butler)
- Butler at Queen's Crawley; went off laughing with Sir Pitt when Sir Pitt seized Rebecca's candle at night

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca Sharp now at Queen's Crawley estate as governess to two daughters; arrived via coach, last part riding outside in rain; now installed at estate with Sir Pitt's household; has been seized by Sir Pitt for candle at night; awaiting life as governess to ten and eight year old girls
